data.title: Stupava – Dračí hrádok, a medieval fort on a Slavic hillfort
data.excerpt: In the cadastral area of Stupava, deep inside the Lesser Carpathians, lie the ruins of a medieval small fort marked on maps as Dračí hrádok: a square tower of 10 × 10 m with walls 2.5 m thick, built in the second half of the 13th century on an older Slavic hillfort. After a destructive fire that followed an armed attack it was never rebuilt, and the defence of the region passed to the nearby castle of Pajštún.
data.metaTitle: Stupava – Dračí hrádok above a Slavic hillfort
data.metaDescription: Ruins of a medieval fort with a square tower (10 × 10 m) of the 13th century on the Úboč spur near Stupava, raised on an older pre-Great Moravian hillfort.

children.text: In the cadastral area of Stupava, but only about 1 km from the last houses of the village of Borinka, lie the ruins of a medieval small fort, marked on maps as
. It lies fairly deep inside the south-western part of the Lesser Carpathians, on a spur of the hill
some 400 m long and 350 m wide at its foot. The difference in height between the surface of the nearby watercourse and the highest point of Dračí hrádok reaches almost 98 m.

children.text: The eminence controlled the route passing from Stupava in the direction of Košiarisko and on towards Lozorno and Svätý Jur. The natural defence of the position was provided on three sides by steep hillsides. The only more passable approach route, above the saddle below the Úboč hill, is to this day cut across by a short earthen bank bent at a right angle, the remains of a collapsed timber-and-earth rampart protected by a ditch set in front of it, which can provisionally be assigned to the pre-Great Moravian to earlier Great Moravian period. Roughly the middle of the promontory is cut by another medieval ditch, about 12 m wide, cut into the rock bedrock and today largely filled in. Beyond it, on a slight eminence approximately 17 m away, are the remains of a massive square tower with external dimensions of 10 × 10 m. It was built of quarry stone bonded with good-quality lime mortar, and the thickness of the walls at the level of the present ground surface reaches 2.5 m. By its function, dimensions and building technology unambiguously a medieval structure, it was the most important masonry defensive building of the fort, perhaps combining in itself the main roles of a donjon (the main residential tower) and of a bergfried (primarily a defensive tower), screening with its mass the residential and farm buildings in the area of the fort from the direction of a presumed attack.

children.text: During the archaeological excavation an almost continuous area of about 370 m² was uncovered behind the tower. According to the archaeological finds, above all pottery, tools, coins and militaria, the small fort evidently came into being in the second half of the 13th century. In the spirit of the defensive doctrine then applied, the area of the original Slavic hillfort was reduced by about half. The greater part of the castle, as with most similar fortifications of the time, consisted of timber log-built buildings, perhaps only single-storeyed, arranged all around above the steep slopes. For reasons of fire protection, aesthetics and thermal insulation their walls were covered with clay plaster. The outer side of the timber buildings, perhaps supplemented by a solid fence in the gaps, evidently also formed the main defensive line above the steep drops into the valley – a defensive wall not otherwise attested. The buildings were probably arranged in such a way that they divided the fortified area into smaller, functionally distinct parts of a farm and of a residential character, with a kitchen partly sunk into the ground close to the residential tower. The circulation space between the presumed kitchen, the tower and the other buildings was formed by a small enclosure, markedly sloping to the west, covered with a poured mortar floor and measuring at least 14 × 11.4 m.

According to the original intention, the timber buildings, above all the defensive wall, were perhaps gradually to be replaced by new masonry architecture, of which, apart from the tower, only part of the western defensive wall has survived. Before the work could advance, the timber houses succumbed to a great fire, in which the clay plaster of the houses was fused into ceramic daub and the originally brown forest soil acquired a rusty-red colouring.

children.text: The numerous and formally very variable arrowheads and other militaria from the area of the fort and from its forefield suggest that the cause of its demise was a direct and evidently successful armed attack. After the destructive fire the small fort was not rebuilt. Life, and the role of defending this region, perhaps passed to the nearby castle of Pajštún, which could thus be the successor of Dračí hrádok.

On the basis of a comparison of the historical reports with the archaeological finds it cannot be ruled out that Dračí hrádok could be the castle of Stupava mentioned in the Klosterneuburg chronicle, which the Czech armies of Přemysl Otakar II occupied almost directly on the march, either on 13 April 1271 or within the next two or three days, and in whose defence comes Alexander perished (

Dračí hrádok thus documents the gradual development of medieval fortifications, moving above all after the Mongol invasion from a timber or timber-and-earth “mini-hillfort” towards a stone castle – a development which was violently interrupted by armed action, and the new masonry fortification then arose in a different place, better suited to the demands of the age and to changing military tactics.

children.text: The easiest way to reach the remains of Dračí hrádok is through the village of Borinka. We drive through the whole village along road no. 1108 and continue straight on along a narrow asphalt road which soon passes through woodland. After about 800 m we come upon an open space beside the track with room for approximately 2 – 3 cars. Here we can park, and directly opposite begins the roughly 15-minute, only moderately demanding climb to the castle along the yellow trail. It is also possible to park a little further on, about 300 – 400 m from the place mentioned along the road, where there is a somewhat larger space for parking.
